body: The best-documented Indian multibaggers fit a few templates. **Turnaround under new management** (Eicher/Royal Enfield). **Policy-shift rerating** (defence PSUs 2020–24, where the move was largely multiple expansion ahead of earnings). **Supply-chain shift** (Deepak Nitrite, China+1). **PLI-led scale** (Dixon). Many of the most recent "fastest wealth creators" were cyclical or policy beneficiaries.
title: multibagger_case_studies › Takeaway

body:
`insight:india-mb-ipo-entry` · confidence: single-source

Ten cases here started at or near an IPO. Low-multiple PSU or out-of-favour listings: HAL (Mar 2018 at ~14x) first fell −56% in two years, then reached ~9x the issue price at its 2024 peak; Cochin Shipyard (2017 issue ≈₹216 adjusted) ~13x at peak; Mazagon (2020, issue ≈₹72.5 adjusted, ~7x P/E) ~48x at peak; CDSL (2017, ≈₹74.5) ~26x; BSE (2017, ≈₹90 adjusted) ~47x. Fairly priced private leaders: Polycab (2019, ~20–27x) ~19x; Dixon (2017, ~60x) ~52x, only because EPS rose ~10x on the PLI scheme. Boom-market listings: Kaynes (2022, ~100x) ~13x at peak and now −62% from it; Waaree (2024, 84x on first close) and Premier (214x) tripled EPS but are below their first close (1.6–1.8x the issue price). Pattern: what matters at listing is the P/E, not the story. Government or out-of-favour IPOs at low multiples left both engines available; hot-sector IPOs at 80x+ left only EPS, and those stocks fell 40–60% at the first stumble. Also, IPO buyers of winners often waited 1–3 years through a −50% drawdown (HAL, Dixon, CDSL). Issue prices here are from general knowledge and should be re-checked (unverified).

Links: `insight:india-mb-starting-pe` (part_of), `case_study:hal-2020-2024` (about), `case_study:kaynes-technology-2022-2026` (about), `case_study:waaree-premier-energies-2024-2026` (about), `case_study:polycab-2019-2026` (about), `case_study:indian-shipyards-2020-2025` (about)

**Version 1.0 · 2026-11-21.** Roadmap stages **5 (valuation)** and **6 (decision)**, with the hand-off to
**stage 7 (scorekeeping)**. Each future deep dive (stage 4) ends by filling these two templates, so every company
comes out with the same comparable fields.
**What it unlocks next:** stage 7 gets one dated, mechanically resolvable set of probabilities per decision
(3 paper calls per card), and stage 1 data (Pi/Kite/Screener) can feed the inputs automatically.
**Not stock picking.** The three companies below are **test material (L9). No verdict, no buy/sell/watchlist
call.** Their scenario inputs are illustrative estimates, chosen to exercise the tools. Research, not
SEBI-registered advice.

| Tool | Path |
|---|---|
| Valuation worksheet | `tools/valuation/worksheet.py` (+ `README.md`, `examples/`) |
| Decision card | `tools/decision/decision_card.py`, template `tools/decision/decision_card.md`, `base_rates.json` (+ `README.md`, `examples/`) |
| memdb seed | `memdb/seeds/2026-11-21_templates.json` (strategy records; not yet ingested) |

Both tools use only the standard library (Python 3.7+), so they run on the Raspberry Pi.

- **Fees** ₹1,168 cr Q2 (1.11% of average earning assets; FY26 1.21% of assets per Ind-Ra): other service charges
  568 (49%), loan processing 246, insurance 146 (Ageas associate), forex/derivatives 104, commissions 104. The CFO
  said some FCNR-related fee is inside but "not significant". Card spends rank 9 among private banks (1.90% spend
  share; 3.13% of cards outstanding, deck slide 28, company calculation).
- **Capital:** CET1 15.76%, RWA ₹2,50,722 cr (density 58.7% of assets). On warrant exercise (+₹4,647 cr) CET1 rises
  ~1.85 pp to ~17.6% [EST] — ROE on diluted book ~10% until deployed. The ₹10,000 cr bond enabling resolution
  (17-Jul-2026) and a USD 500 mn MTN programme (17-Sep-2026) add funding options. M&A rumours: Jana SFB
  (25-Sep-2026) and "open to deals" (19-Oct-2026), both answered "no material event".
- **Digital partnerships risk:** the deck lists partner channels for deposits, loans, cards, merchant payments and
  remittance; the AR notes "resumption of business with a key fintech partner" (i.e. it had paused). Partner names,
  the share of cards/deposits sourced through partners and any RBI direction are **not disclosed** → ground check.
